hints: Follow each alkene through its two-step story, first what addition or cleavage happens, then what oxidation level is reached.
Ethene plus steam gives ethanol, and heating a primary alcohol under reflux with acidified dichromate(VI) pushes oxidation all the way to a 2-carbon carboxylic acid.
Hot, concentrated manganate(VII) cleaves the C=C bond in but-2-ene, so count the carbons in each fragment and identify its functional group to compare with X.
walkthrough:
**Find X from ethene**

Think hydration first, then strong oxidation. Ethene adds steam to make ethanol, a primary alcohol.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Oxidise ethanol under reflux**

Reflux with acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ means full oxidation, not stopping at the aldehyde. A primary alcohol goes to aldehyde then to carboxylic acid.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2[\text{O}] \xrightarrow{\text{reflux}} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So X is ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, with 2 carbons.

**Find Y from but-2-ene**

Hot, concentrated, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ does vigorous oxidative cleavage of the double bond. Each $\text{C}=\text{C}$ carbon becomes a carboxylic acid carbon.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 + 4[\text{O}] \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. } \text{MnO}_4^- / \text{H}^+} 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
So Y is also ethanoic acid, with 2 carbons per molecule.

**Compare X and Y**

Both X and Y are $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$. They have the same number of carbon atoms and the same carboxylic acid functional group. They are the same compound.

options.A: Incorrect. X is ethanoic acid with 2 carbons, and each molecule of Y is also ethanoic acid with 2 carbons, so X does not have more carbons.
options.B: Incorrect. Although but-2-ene starts with 4 carbons, cleavage splits it into two 2-carbon molecules. One molecule of Y therefore has the same carbon count as X, not more.
options.C: Incorrect. Both X and Y are carboxylic acids ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$). Students sometimes think cleavage gives a ketone or aldehyde, but hot concentrated conditions give the acid.
options.D: Correct. X from ethanol oxidation is ethanoic acid, and Y from oxidative cleavage of but-2-ene is also ethanoic acid. Same formula, same functional group, same compound.
